findings.finding: The accepted plan replaces the tuple-less IPreparedScanPairBuilder.BuildAsync shape and requires exact-tuple coordinator composition, but the tasks assign no writable owner for existing Prepared Scan tests that directly call the old builder signature or assert the old production graph.
findings.recommended_correction: Add an explicit dependency-ordered compatibility RED/update/verification slice owned by the exclusive Prepared Scan integration-test owner. Name every affected existing test file, update only fixture/composition calls to construct and pass the immutable initiation tuple and assert the new initiation coordinator graph, preserve all existing behavioral assertions, and forbid retaining a tuple-less production overload merely to keep tests compiling.

findings.finding: The plan requires the current analysis health probe and Prepared Scan initiation to share one extracted configured-integrity/runtime-identity implementation, but no task explicitly authorizes the semantic delegation/extraction needed in the existing ConfiguredAnalysisRuntimeHealthProbe.
evidence: src/dotnet/Vulgata.Web/Program.cs:560-735 currently owns the configured CodeGraph/JDT-LS integrity checks and constructs AnalysisRuntimeIdentity internally.
The current health result exposes the identity hash, not the complete canonical analysis-runtime/1 JSON required by initiation.
T022 permits only three new Web files and T024 limits Program.cs to registrations and compile-only adjustments.
findings.recommended_correction: Amend T020-T024 so the exclusive Program.cs integration owner extracts or delegates ConfiguredAnalysisRuntimeHealthProbe integrity/identity construction to ConfiguredPreparedScanRuntimeIdentityResolver. Characterize identical health behavior and hashes, complete per-Repository runtime JSON/hash, and no duplicated integrity algorithm.

findings.finding: T015 requires an injected commit failure to expose zero rows, while the accepted plan and contract guarantee rollback only for failures before commit; a genuine client-visible commit failure may be outcome-ambiguous.
evidence: T015 separately expands the accepted pre-commit rollback guarantee to commit failure with zero rows.
findings.recommended_correction: Use an explicitly injected pre-commit transaction failure proving zero rows, or test ambiguous-commit recovery as unavailable followed by exact retry materializing or replaying the one canonical tuple.

coverage_summary.declared_coverage: All FR-001 through FR-078 and SC-001 through SC-025 have declared owners, but the compatibility and runtime ownership gaps prevent deterministic execution.

task_order_and_ownership_assessment.overall: The public RED, Core, PostgreSQL, tuple handoff, authorization/runtime, composition, regression, convergence, quality, and run-03 ordering is otherwise coherent.
task_order_and_ownership_assessment.blocking_issue: Known affected compatibility tests and the semantic health-probe refactor lack writable owners.

prohibited_boundary_confirmation: All prohibited CGC, legacy profiling, general Scan, EF/model, Story 12.4, Track A/B, security, fake evidence, retained database, later-stage, and transaction boundaries remain preserved.

implementation_approval_scope_summary.reason: Correct DR-PSI-001 through DR-PSI-003 and obtain a fresh independent ACCEPT.
implementation_approval_scope_summary.eventual_production_scope: The bounded exactly-two-Repository Prepared Scan initiation implementation and tests only.

rationale: REVISE. The specification and accepted plan are coherent and feasible, but tasks omit mandatory compatibility ownership, omit the shared runtime-identity semantic owner, and overstate one transaction failure guarantee.
